specification.problem: Identify a Boolean function f:{0,1}^n->{0,1} that is linear, f(x)=a.x, or affine, f(x)=a.x xor b, using one oracle query (BV) or two queries, with certainty for fully specified functions; the incompletely defined case is only noted.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny instance n=2 with standard phase-oracle BV (one query) for linear f, plus an assumed two-query affine identification that runs BV and then a second query on the all-zero input to read off b. Incompletely defined functions, the 2/3 bounded-error analysis, the specific classes of partial functions, and the paper's actual two-query construction are outside the scope.

symbols.domain: positive integer; n=2 in the tiny instance

equations.label: Affine function form
equations.description: Linear functions correspond to b=0; affine functions allow arbitrary b.
equations.abstract_quote: if the provided Boolean function is affine
equations.justification: The abstract refers to linear and affine Boolean functions; the standard definition of these is used for the explicit form.
assumptions: Standard definition of affine Boolean function over GF(2)

equations.label: Phase oracle
equations.description: Oracle convention used in the construction.
equations.justification: The abstract does not specify the oracle form; the phase oracle is the common choice.
assumptions: Phase-oracle form rather than a bit-flip oracle with ancilla

equations.label: BV output state
equations.description: One query yields a with certainty, up to a global phase (-1)^b that is unobservable, so b is not recovered.
equations.justification: Standard BV derivation using the identity sum_x (-1)^{a.x xor y.x} = 2^n delta_{a,y}.

equations.label: Offset from f(0)
equations.description: Given a, the offset is the value of f at the zero input. A second query, e.g. a phase kickback or interference measurement, can determine it.
equations.justification: A simple construction consistent with the abstract's claim that one more query is needed for affinity, but it is not the paper's stated method.
assumptions: The second query is used to extract b; the exact circuit is not given in the abstract

equations.label: Success threshold for incomplete functions
equations.description: The bounded-error success criterion for the incompletely defined case.
equations.abstract_quote: with probability of success at least $2/3$
equations.justification: Stated directly in the abstract; the classes of functions for which it holds are not specified.

registers.name: x
registers.role: input register carrying the query, initial |0^n>

registers.name: anc
registers.role: possible ancilla or control qubit for the second query

specification.initial_state: |0^n> on the input register, in the n=2 instance |00>

steps.description: Query 1 (BV): apply H^{\otimes n}, then U_f, then H^{\otimes n}, and measure in the computational basis to obtain a.
Query 2 (assumed): determine b=f(0^n) by a second query using an interference or control construction. The details are not specified in the abstract.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the input register after the BV circuit gives a; the second measurement gives b under the assumed construction.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Output f(x)=a.x xor b; the affine versus linear decision is b=1 versus b=0 (that is, f is linear iff b=0).
assumptions: Second-query circuit is a placeholder, not the paper's method
missing_information: Definition of the incompletely defined function classes
Oracle model used in the paper
